name: csv-read
algorithm: Read one log file (the generated input, 50 MB of lines of seven space-separated unquoted fields) as CSV records with the delimiter space, through each standard library's CSV reader over a buffered file reader of 64 KiB, r times; prints the records, the fields and the field bytes (Mk std.csv Records over fs.File.Reader, Go encoding/csv over bufio.Reader).

skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the counts, which stay below 2^33
skip.c: no std CSV reader in C; the hand-written reader plan/08-m8.md 4.18 asks for, labelled, is a stand-in, which this table forbids (tests/bench/README.md 'No stand-ins'), so it is kept outside the row in ../standin/ for a labelled table (requested of bench8 in status/std-csv.md, review finding csv-4)
skip.rust: Rust std has no CSV reader; the csv crate (the plan's Rust peer) is not std, so it would be a stand-in here too, and it needs cargo and a crate, which tools/bench does not build (its Rust cells are single rustc files): requested of bench8 with the labelled table in status/std-csv.md
skip.zig: no std CSV reader in Zig

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the record, field and byte counts check that every reader split the file the same way
notes: The input is std-regex's (same kind, size and seed), so tools/bench generates it once. It holds no quote, so the row measures the unquoted path: the search for the delimiter and the line break.

The ratio that counts is Mk against Go's encoding/csv, the only other standard library with a CSV reader. Mk's Record.Field checks each field's UTF-8 (a str); encoding/csv makes one string per record and checks nothing.
C left the row in review round 1 (finding csv-4): its cell was a hand-written reader that built no field value, unequal work in a table of standard libraries.
Written by std-csv, M8, 2026-11-12; checksums from the Go column's run.
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
